claim: For every finite projective plane \(\Pi\) of order \(q\ge 2\), if \(G_\Pi\) is its incidence graph with the shortest-path metric, then \(\mathrm{VR}(G_\Pi;2)\simeq\bigvee^{q^3}S^2\). Consequently its positive-dimensional Vietoris–Rips persistence has exactly \(q^3\) degree-\(1\) bars with birth \(1\) and death \(2\), exactly \(q^3\) degree-\(2\) bars with birth \(2\) and death \(3\), and no other positive-dimensional bars.
integrity: The proof and executable checks are separated: finite computations corroborate the theorem but are not used as evidence for the universal quantifier.
scientific_limitations: The general theorem is proved from the projective-plane axioms. Executable finite checks cover only the Desarguesian orders 2 and 3, and no claim is made for broader incidence geometries or weighted metrics.
title: Scale-two Vietoris–Rips complexes of finite projective-plane incidence graphs
